evals.name: choose-source
evals.prompt: I'm writing a 10-step tutorial with four long code blocks, and one five-line illustration in an explanation page. How should the code for each be sourced and kept from drifting? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Long tutorial: a buildable sample or spec maintained with the product; extract displayed snippets from it, or keep a reproducible extraction or snippet-equality check run with the build in CI. Manual comparison is a one-time review, not a drift guard. Short illustration: the smallest self-contained block, every type and signature verified against first-party source at the supported version, with assumed setup stated.
assertions: Recommends a buildable sample or spec maintained with the product for the long tutorial, with snippets extracted from it.
Says that without extraction tooling a reproducible snippet-equality check should run with the sample build in CI, and that manual comparison is only a one-time review, not a drift guard.
Says the five-line illustration does not need a new sample repository but must have every framework type and signature verified against first-party source at the supported version.
Says the illustration should state the domain types or setup it assumes rather than presenting a partial excerpt as a standalone app.

evals.name: compiles-but-fails
evals.prompt: The TypeScript tab of our docs example compiles, but at runtime the live query never updates. The plan is to ship it and add a note in the prose saying 'a refresh may be needed'. Also the build is green, so we say it's verified. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: A compiling tab is not a working tab. Confirm discovery/registration, proxy generation and runtime behavior against a real kernel and sink. Do not publish code that fails at runtime with a prose workaround; put working code in the tab and reference the tracking issue in a code comment. A rendered fence or green site build is not compilation or behavior proof.
assertions: Says a compiling tab is not a working tab and that claimed runtime behavior such as live updates must be observed against a real kernel and sink.
Says not to publish code that fails at runtime with a workaround in the prose after it.
Says to put working code in the tab and reference the tracking issue in a code comment.
Says a rendered code fence or green docs build proves syntax highlighting, not compilation or behavior.

evals.name: validator-scope
evals.prompt: The Arc client snippet validator reported '38 snippets passed' on our PR, which also changes ordinary Markdown code fences in a product guide. A teammate says the guide's code is therefore verified. Is that right? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: No. The validator checks supported C# fences in Documentation/client-snippets/**; check the reported count and exclusions, since unsupported markers or legacy snippets are not proved compilable. It does not compile ordinary Markdown/MDX fences elsewhere; verify those against real source and a runnable sample/spec or explicit snippet comparison.
assertions: Says the validator covers supported C# fences in Documentation/client-snippets and does not compile ordinary Markdown or MDX fences elsewhere in product docs.
Says to check the validator's reported count and exclusions because unsupported markers or legacy snippets are not proved compilable by a passing run.
Says the guide's fences should be verified against real source and a runnable sample, spec or explicit snippet comparison.
Does not claim coverage from a site build or a validator that never scans the page.

evals.name: multi-language-tabs
evals.prompt: We have a C# example and need to add a Kotlin tab. The Kotlin client doesn't exist yet for this feature, and the tabs name the id type differently (Guid vs String). A teammate suggests translating the C# call by hand and explaining in prose which name each tab uses. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Do not translate a C# call by guess; offer only implementations that exist, compiled against their own SDK, using the established client-owned snippet mechanism. Use the same domain type names in every tab; if prose must explain names, fix the snippets. State each backend's id and response wire type and keep one id type per concept across a series.
assertions: Refuses to hand-translate the C# call and says to offer only implementations that exist, compiled against their own SDK.
Says to use the same domain type names in every tab and to fix the snippets instead of explaining names in prose.
Says to state each backend's id and command-response wire type and keep one id type per concept across every page of a series.
